subject: Joint modeling question: shared fixed effect as well as random effects

messages.author: ede8ea344df4b430
messages.subject: Joint modeling question: shared fixed effect as well as random effects
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to using INLA to fit a joint model of longitudinal and survival models. Those two models are connected by sharing some same fixed effect and random effects, for example,

The longitudinal model is:
Y_ij = Xi'beta + Hij'delta + Ui'Zij, 
where i stands for subject and j stands for jth measure within ith subject and  Xi = (Xi1, Xi2)and Hij =(Hi1, Hi2*tj) are fixed effects, Ui is the subject specific random effects (two dimensional) and Zij = c(1, tj),

The survival model is:
h(Ti) = h0(Ti)*exp(-Wi'gamma + alpha1*H'_{iTi}delta + alpha2*Ui'Zi), 
where we can set h0(Ti) =1 for simplicity and W is fixed effect only for the survival model.

I saw the post for coding the model only when there is only shared random effects, using the copy method, but not shared fixed effects, can anyone help to show me how to construct the formula for this joint model under INLA?

Any help is greatly appreciated!

Thanks,
Ming

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Joint modeling question: shared fixed effect as well as random effects
parts:
On Fri, 2015-01-09 at 20:39 -0800, Ming Yang wrote:


> I saw the post for coding the model only when there is only shared
> random effects, using the copy method, but not shared fixed effects,
> can anyone help to show me how to construct the formula for this joint
> model under INLA?

sharing a fixed effect does not involve any complications if the 'beta'
is the same, like

eta.1 = ... + beta * x.1 + ...
eta.2 = ... + beta * x.2 + ...


H

eta2 = ...+ alpha*(beta*x) + ...

how do we formulate this? do we use the f() function?
